hypothesis: Promotion success requires candidate identity acknowledgment from the runtime, and an interrupted or unverified publication must fence the same loop before further hook access even without a durable journal.
positive_controls: valid publication with real SQLite journal and signed checkpoint evidence
primary_properties: no terminal success events after publication failure
no hook access or rollout step after failure
original cancellation propagated for unjournaled caller cancellation
prepared or committed durable evidence retained for independent reconciliation
acceptance: Pinned baseline has 10 semantic failures and 2 positive-control passes; candidate passes all 12 with no setup errors or skips. Existing discard and checkpoint-bound promotion checks remain passing.
budget: CPU fixtures and real local SQLite only; no model downloads, accelerator, paid API, or confirmation tasks; 30-second comparison subprocess limit.
stopping_rule: Retain the first baseline and matched candidate comparison. Preserve any negative result; do not modify observed outcome-bearing criteria.
limits: One loop in one process with trusted hooks; identity acknowledgment is not checkpoint authentication. Durable checkpoint binding remains opt-in. No multi-host atomicity, detached-worker termination, hard cancellation deadline, or model-quality improvement is claimed.
